chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Hashimi, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Al-Wassah, who said: Najiyyah ibn Al-Harith Al-Attar narrated to me.

He said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the fasting of the day of Ashura, and he said: It is a discontinued fast with the descent of the month of Ramadan, and that which is discontinued is an innovation.
Najiyyah said: Then I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that after his father, and he answered me with the same answer as his father.

Then he said: Indeed, it is the fasting of a day for which no Book was revealed and no Sunnah was established, except the Sunnah of the family of Ziyad regarding the killing of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.سُنَّةُ آلِ زِيَادٍ: Sunnah of the family of Ziyad
key_terms.صَوْمُ يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ: Fasting of the day of Ashura

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the day of Ashura according to Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* establishes the jurisprudential ruling that fasting on Ashura is a pre-Islamic or early Islamic practice abrogated by the obligation of Ramadan, rendering it a *bid'ah* (innovation) if performed as a standalone act of worship. The Imam’s clarification that it lacks specific scriptural revelation (*kitab*) or established prophetic precedent (*sunnah*) distinguishes it from the commemorative fasting of the Ahl al-Bayt, which is rooted in the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (AS) rather than divine command. This highlights the Shia distinction between ritual fasting for reward and fasting for commemoration or gratitude.
